item.title: Kerry Co-op Creameries assuring suppliers they'll have ample time to consider new milk supply contracts
item.description: Kerry Co-operative Creameries is assuring suppliers that they'll have ample time to consider new milk supply contracts before they must be signed. The current contracts are valid until the end of April. Interim chair of the Munster Dairy Producer Organisation (MDPO), James Doyle says milk suppliers have been promised a draft of the new contract many times, but that these target dates have come and gone, with no contract circulated to farmers. item.title: Man taken to hospital after fire broke out in Killarney
item.description: A man was taken to hospital after a fire broke out in Killarney last evening. The blaze occurred at St Michael’s Halting Site on the Killarney bypass, close to the fire station. A unit at the halting site went on fire. Advertisement Two fire-fighting appliances attended the blaze at around quarter to seven. A man in the unit was brought to University Hospital Kerry. item.title: Over €6.7 million paid out in vacant property refurbishment grants in Kerry to date
item.description: Over €6.7 million has been paid out in Vacant Property Refurbishment Grants to bring homes in Kerry back into use since its induction. That’s according to figures from the Department of Housing, which show more than €246 million has been paid out under the scheme nationally since it was launched in 2022. Over 120 vacant homes in Kerry have been brought back into use over this period. Advertisement Kerry Fine Gael Senator Mike Kennelly, and Fianna Fáil TD Michael Cahill have welcomed the figures.

item.title: Last two winners among entries for Stayers' Hurdle
item.description: The last two winners of the Stayers' Hurdle, Teahupoo and Bob Olinger, remain among the entries for the day three feature of the Cheltenham Festival next week. item.title: Ireland South MEP calls for ban on anonymous social media accounts in the EU
item.description: An Ireland South MEP has called for a ban to anonymous social media accounts in the EU. Billy Kelleher made the plea during a European Parliament debate on cyber bulling. The Fianna Fáil MEP says measures need to be introduced, adding an ID for users needs to be stored and verified by platforms. Advertisement He says keyboard warriors and those from outside the EU should stop trying to impose their country’s legal system onto Europe. item.title: HSE delivered almost 900,000 home help hours in Kerry last year
item.description: The HSE provided almost 900,000 (896,287) home help hours in Kerry last year. At the end of December, more than 2,300 (2,326) clients were receiving the HSE’s home support service in Kerry, with 28 clients waiting to access the service for the first time. This represents an 88% drop in the number of people waiting compared with three years ago. item.title: €4 million allocated to accelerate retrofitting of social homes in Kerry
item.description: €4 million euro in funding has been announced to accelerate the retrofitting of social homes in Kerry. This funding was announced by Minister for Housing James Browne. It has been welcomed by Independent TD Danny Healy-Rae, Fine Gael senator Mike Kennelly and Fianna Fáil TD Michael Cahill.
